summary.text:
Waltham Forest's 2026-27 Treasury Management Strategy went to Full Council on 26 February 2026. What ModernGov holds under document 106964 is the covering report only — four pages, no numbers. The substance sits in Appendix 1, referenced repeatedly (MRP policy on pages 19–20, prudential indicators, borrowing and investment strategy on pages 21–27), but Appendix 1 is a separate ModernGov document we do not hold. The parallel report to Audit and Governance Committee five days earlier (document 106811) is the same four-page cover, so pulling that sibling did not fill the gap.

What the covering report itself carries is short. Para 4.1 states the Council is maintaining an under-borrowed position — CFR not fully funded with loan debt, reserves and cash flow used as a temporary measure. Para 4.2 sets investment priorities as security first, liquidity second, then yield. Para 5.1 names MUFG Corporate Markets as treasury adviser (the rebrand of Link Asset Services after the 2024 sale). Para 6.2.1 refers to the S151 as the Strategic Director of Resources without naming them, and the Contact Officer block on page 1 names Debbie Drew (Assistant Director of Pensions and Treasury) and Zainab Roberts (Treasury Manager), both with published council email addresses.

No loan-book reconciliation is possible against this paper — there is no printed table for our figures to tie to. No balance-sheet identity check is possible either — CFR, external borrowing and other long-term liabilities are all in Appendix 1. Our PWLB record for Waltham Forest is held internally in the note (see the internal block below), machine-checked at 16 August 2026 against the DMO record via price_book.py, and kept out of the email entirely per PIPELINE.md.

Draft is written in the North Norfolk mould: acknowledges the covering-only scope up front, quotes nothing about the Council's position, offers market context and platform links, and directs the reader to /loan-analysis where our PWLB file is visible. Contacts are Zainab Roberts and Debbie Drew, both taken verbatim from the covering report — the S151 name is not published in the paper and is not invented. Meeting anchor for the send-by is the Audit & Governance Committee on 14 October 2026, the typical mid-year treasury review slot.

Para 6.2.1 refers to the S151 by title only; no name is printed in the covering report. Do not invent — take the S151's name from a paper that prints it before adding to the recipient line.

officer.body:
Hi Zainab,

Apologies for the cold email. PWLBtoday is fairly new so you may not have come across us yet.

We're built for local authority treasury teams and nothing else: live PWLB rates at both daily fixings, a monthly breakdown of every loan the sector draws, every council's PWLB book priced daily against the DMO's repayment curve, and a training academy for officers and members. There's more — the predictor, the SONIA path, peer metrics, a daily brief — in the brochure at [BROCHURE URL]. We don't sell treasury products, and the data side is free and stays free.

To keep that data and our training relevant we built tools that watch committee papers across every council in the country, so we can see how a council's own figures compare with where the market has gone since. Normally that means we write with something specific about a council's own numbers. This one is shorter and more honest than most, because what reached us under document 106964 is the covering report to your 2026-27 Treasury Management Strategy — four pages — not Appendix 1, which is where the MRP policy on pages 19 to 20, the prudential indicators, and the Treasury Management Strategy Statement and Annual Investment Strategy on pages 21 to 27 all sit. So nothing below is a comment on your position, and we haven't guessed at one. You're not being singled out — every authority gets one of these — and there's no agenda in it.

What the covering report itself carries is the strategic framing: paragraph 4.1 that you're maintaining an under-borrowed position with reserves, balances and cash flow used as a temporary measure, security-first-then-liquidity-then-yield on the investment side at 4.2, and MUFG Corporate Markets on the adviser line at 5.1. That's your language, not ours, and the scale is what Appendix 1 quantifies. Where we can be useful for now is on the other half — the market you're pricing your under-borrowed decision against. Bank Rate is 3.75%, one-year PWLB certainty closed at 4.95% this afternoon on notice 314/26, and July's sector borrowing was £368m across 33 loans from just 19 borrowers at an average 5.02%. If it helps to see what we hold for Waltham Forest on the PWLB side while Appendix 1 is the authoritative version, pwlbtoday.org/loan-analysis is that view, and pwlbtoday.org/pwlb-activity is the monthly sector draw.

One standing pointer, unrelated to the gap in what we hold: the interactive liability benchmark pathway at pwlbtoday.org/liability-benchmark is worth a look ahead of CIPFA's forthcoming updates to the Prudential and Treasury Codes, and particularly for a council whose stated position is under-borrowed — it's the indicator most likely to matter to that framing. Live data, and it plots against the councils we've read that publish theirs.

On the caveats: we hold PWLB only — LOBOs, market debt, bank loans and inter-authority borrowing all sit outside our file. Any break-cost figure we publish is indicative only against the DMO's premature repayment curve; only the DMO's own quote is binding. We model no MRP or accounting treatment.

On training, three courses fit even without the appendix. Liability Benchmark: the essentials, given the under-borrowed framing. Prudential Indicators for members, since 1 to 7 go to Council directly for approval. And Money Market Funds (CNAV / LVNAV / VNAV) on the investment side. All 115 courses are free to local authorities until the end of September at pwlbtoday.org/academy, and free accounts for the whole team.

And if you do find it useful, mentioning it to others would help us more than anything. We're small, word of mouth is most of our marketing, and every sign-up helps us prove the need.

Sign up free → https://pwlbtoday.org/
Follow on LinkedIn → https://www.linkedin.com/company/pwlbtoday/

Russell
https://www.linkedin.com/in/russelltew
